issues.description: The template's test support header defaults FIX_LEN to 4 (32-bit fixed type), while the example program and the solution's tests expect FIX_LEN to be 8 (64-bit fixed type). This macro controls the typedef for fix_t and therefore the binary interfaces and expected numeric ranges in tests. The mismatch will cause type/size inconsistencies between the tests and the example/assignment code and can lead to incorrect test behavior or compilation/linking problems for students.
issues.suggestedFix: Make FIX_LEN consistent across the template repositories: set the default FIX_LEN in tests/src/math_fix.h to 8 to match example_program/src/math_fix.c and the solution tests, or clearly document and provide a single place (common header) to configure FIX_LEN. Ensure all test expectations and typedefs use the same FIX_LEN value so fix_t has a consistent size for students' implementations.

issues.description: The fixed-point configuration macro FIX_LEN (the conceptual 'length of fixed-point number in bytes') is inconsistent between the test harness and the example program in the template repository: tests default FIX_LEN to 4 while the example program uses FIX_LEN = 8. This mismatches the same conceptual entity across artifacts and will confuse students about which fixed-point size to target (and may cause compilation/behavior differences between tests and the example). The solution repository uses FIX_LEN = 8 consistently, so the template tests are the outlier.
issues.suggestedFix: Standardize the FIX_LEN default across all artifacts. Update tests/src/math_fix.h in the template repository to match the example program (change #define FIX_LEN 4 to #define FIX_LEN 8) or centralize the FIX_LEN definition in a single header included by both the example and tests. Also document the chosen FIX_LEN in problem_statement.md so students know which fixed-point size is expected.
